subcategory: video RAG over a probabilistic temporal knowledge graph
problem: Existing RAG methods fail to jointly encode multimodal and long-range temporal information and use static text matching that cannot align queries with the right video segments.
architecture: ViG-RAG: videos split into 30-second segments, captioned by a VLM and transcribed by ASR; a probabilistic temporal knowledge graph of quintuples (head, relation, tail, time, plausibility) is built; semantic-temporal dual-level retrieval with a training-free Gaussian-mixture filter that picks high-confidence segments, LLM-guided query-aware re-ranking, and a VLM that generates the answer from anchors, context and selected frames.
retriever: text-embedding-3-small over entities/passages + ImageBind multimodal embeddings, GMM-based adaptive top-K
generator: GPT-4o-mini orchestration; MiniCPM-V; plug-in for Video-LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT-Video, LongVA, Long-LLaVA, Qwen2-VL, LLaVA-Video
knowledge_source: video transcripts, captions and frames organised in a temporal knowledge graph

datasets.name: LongerVideos
datasets.details: more than twenty video sets (lecture, documentary, entertainment)

datasets.name: Video-MME
datasets.details: clips from 11 seconds to nearly an hour

key_results: LongerVideos overall win rate 41.77% vs 35.81% for VideoRAG and 22.42% for GraphRAG-local in three-way judging.
Video-MME overall: LLaVA-NeXT-Video improves from 43.0 to 54.2 (+11.2) and Qwen2-VL-72B from 64.9 to 72.4 when ViG-RAG is plugged in.
LLaVA-Video-72B with ViG-RAG reaches 74.4 overall, adding about 2.1K text tokens per example.
strengths: Model-agnostic plug-in that improves six open-source VLMs of 7B and 72B size.
Joint temporal and semantic indexing with adaptive (threshold-free) evidence selection.

limitations.text: Main comparison relies on LLM-as-judge win rates (GPT-4o-mini), which can be biased.
Pipeline depends on several large models (VLM captioning, ASR, GPT-4o-mini), increasing indexing cost; no cost analysis in the excerpted results.

notes: Five independent judging trials with randomised answer order.
title: ViG-RAG: Video-aware Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Temporal and Semantic Hybrid Reasoning
